quote: $\log W = \sum N_i \log N_i$ = Maximum bei den Nebenbed.
english: log W = sum of N_i log N_i = maximum under the side conditions (sum of i N_i = n, sum of N_i = N, with multipliers lambda and mu).
topic: Notes on using a mean-free-path-type method to solve an integral equation, on the role of experiment and the axiomatic method in mathematics versus physics, a speculative remark on the second law of thermodynamics and perpetual motion of the second kind, and the start of a statistical (Boltzmann-type) maximization for the distribution of molecular energies.

triage.modern_statement: This is not an open research problem. It is the standard combinatorial calculation from statistical mechanics. N molecules are spread over discrete energy levels i (energy proportional to i), with N_i molecules at level i. The task is to find the occupation numbers {N_i} that maximize the number of microstates W = N!/∏N_i!. Using Stirling's formula, log W ≈ const − Σ N_i log N_i, so the problem is to extremize Σ N_i log N_i (maximize −Σ N_i log N_i) subject to Σ N_i = N and Σ i N_i = n (fixed total energy), with Lagrange multipliers μ and λ. The answer is the Boltzmann (geometric/exponential) distribution N_i ∝ e^{−λ i}. The sign in the transcription ('log W = Σ N_i log N_i = Maximum') is either Hilbert's shorthand or a transcription slip; the correct expression has a minus sign.
triage.answered_by: Ludwig Boltzmann, 1877: 'Über die Beziehung zwischen dem zweiten Hauptsatze der mechanischen Wärmetheorie und der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung respektive den Sätzen über das Wärmegleichgewicht', Wiener Berichte 76, pp. 373–435. This was before Hilbert's note, so Hilbert was reworking a known derivation, probably for lectures or study. English translation by K. Sharp and F. Matschinsky, Entropy 17 (2015) 1971–2009. The Lagrange-multiplier version is now textbook material.

evidence.claim: Boltzmann's 1877 paper in the Sitzungsberichte of the Vienna Academy (vol. 76, pp. 373–435) gives the probability-based combinatorial treatment of thermal equilibrium. It was reprinted in his Wissenschaftliche Abhandlungen in 1909.
Sharp and Matschinsky (Entropy, 2015) describe this paper as the first to establish the probabilistic basis of entropy, and the paper in which the Boltzmann distribution first appears.
The most probable occupancy is found by maximizing the weight W of a configuration, using Lagrange multipliers for the particle-number and energy constraints. This is standard textbook material.
Boltzmann's setup: N particles, cells with energies ε_n, occupation numbers w_n; maximize the multiplicity under constraints.

triage.why: The expression and the two side conditions (Σ N_i = N and Σ i N_i = n, with multipliers μ and λ) match Boltzmann's 1877 maximization over discrete energy levels exactly. That calculation was published decades before Hilbert's notebook entry and gives the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution. It is not among Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. Hilbert's 6th problem (axiomatizing physics, including probability and kinetic theory) is related in spirit, but this particular entry is a standard derivation, not a new question. As a variational problem it is fully solved and is not an active research topic.
